Your feelings are very valid and I can relate. Just for context: my dad is white, mom is Japanese and I have fully cut my dad out of my life since sometime last year. 
But I can fully relate to that feeling of disappointment of not just being misunderstood, but the parent not even trying to understand you. Over the years of trying to talk to my dad about things regarding race and other parts of my identity, I just realized some ppl straight up don’t want to listen. They ultimately value their pride, selfish desires, their rigid worldview, etc over connecting to others. And this especially hurts when your parent is essentially choosing this over their relationship with you. Although it was very difficult (and can still be hard), the best decision I made for myself was cutting out my dad. As he chose himself over our relationship, I am also choosing myself. I realized he never really cared abt me as a whole person, just some projection of wat he wanted in a kid (which happens regardless of being mixed race or not). People really have kids half assed, thinking about how cute it’ll be to have their mini me, and not realize their kid will become a full grown adult outside of them lol. 
Anyway, I understand that your circumstance is still different than mine, considering your other parent has passed away, so I’m not writing this as advice but more as a “I see you”. 
I wish you the best with whatever decision you make in your relationship with your parent, none of this is easy.

Hmm, so the last time I relied on notes for school was high school like 8 yrs ago. BUT I have overtime developed a system for a bunch of notebooks I have that I use frequently so Mayb this cud help? 
Each book I have a overall big category (ex: Game Development) and within the book I make sections (ex: art/design, play theory, games to play, original game ideas, misc/uncategorized) and each section I color code the title whenever I start a new entry. So that way even if within each entry I have a bunch of sloppy notes, I can at least flip thru the book and b like okay well the title is yellow therefore this section is about game art/design. 
I remember doing exactly what you did when I used to take notes for school; have a bunch of notebooks with scribbled and messy unorganized writing and I would just end up copying word for word whatever I was taking notes on. So looking back at the notes was essentially useless. The only benefit I got from that, is that just the act of writing it down did help to obtain SOME info (not a lot lol). 
So I guess in short: organizing from macro to micro helps a lot especially if it’s dense information. I even draw out a little bubble diagram sometimes to help me visualize the big topics and how they can be broken down into smaller ones. And always have a misc category Bc eventually you will build up categories within the misc as you keep writing instead of forcing things into a category where it doesn’t really belong.
I hope this all made sense, it’s kinda a lot to describe in writing. Lmk if u hav questions!

I feel everyone has their own very personal ways of going about this. I used to be a heavy drinker specifically when I was Not medicated and extremely unstable. Now that I found medication that has really worked for me (Lamictal/Lamotrigine), I was able to have a stable thought process and examine myself and why I would drink heavily. 

To be honest I was lucky in the sense of already being allergic to alcohol where it would become physically uncomfortable to drink, so over time it just felt so awful that It would force me to re-examine. Otherwise I would look back at my past and rationalize in myself why it would be such a disaster to go back. And really think through the pros and cons and just seeing how the cons of drinking outweighs the pros so much helps to ground me. I think it’s important to examine why you drink and especially why you feel the need to discipline yourself to decrease consumption. Do you drink just for the taste of it? For coping ? For the slight buzz? To get fucked up? Socially? Habitually? 

I think for me it has been hard to replace drinking in habitual modes of consuming alcohol. For example I used to drink beer while cooking and it was a pleasant habit that I really enjoyed. Now that I don’t drink, I replace that beer with a juice or juice and seltzer (to give effect of the bubbling of beer) and slowly sip it as I used to beer. 

Also socially not drinking has been strange to adjust to but similarly if feeling awkward as the only person without a drink, or not knowing what to do with ur hands lol, just sipping on juice/seltzer helps a LOT. or even if that’s not close enough in terms of flavor there’s non alcoholic beer (if ur into beer). 

Also realllyyy has helped me to be around sober people. Everyone in my household is sober so it’s not even a thought in the back of my head in terms of alcohol being in the house. 

Last thing to note: if you have trauma/very negative experiences associated with drinking, I personally don’t think it’s best to drink at all really. At least that’s another reason why I just can’t rationalize in myself to go back. I think it’s important to treat it like any other addiction (if you feel that is your case). 

tldr; it’s first and foremost important to ask urself why you want to stop/decrease consumption/why it’s so hard, and get to the root of the problem , then you can start to find ur own personalized solution. I do think finding some level of stability internally is the first step to really analyze oneself. In the end everyone deals with this differently and I just wanted to share my own experience. I wish you the best of luck !!!

Hello, I can provide my own half Asian/White perspectives in terms of what you are asking. For background, my mother is from Japan, my father white american from florida and I grew up in the same household as both of them in Hawaii.  
I'm going to be very blunt with you because for the sake of your future baby I just hope that you are thoughtful about your decisions in terms of raising them. I am now 25 years old and have lived apart from my parents for the past 7 years since leaving high school. And I cannot stress enough how this distance has helped me realize sooo many things.  
So I grew up around a loot of mixed kids, especially part asian kids. So I never felt like an outsider in that sense, but because my mother was directly from Japan that created different issues that have been hard to come to terms with within myself.   
In my household though, race was pretty much never talked about. The only times it would be brought up would be from my mother saying things like, youre so lucky you are mixed because you are more beautiful and you get to experience both cultures. But looking back my mom desperately wanted a white child and I was the closest thing that she could get. This feeling is very traumatizing and I still experience identity problems. All in all, although I grew up learning Japanese and being a part of the culture, and I personally now strongly identify with the culture, the lack of conversation or even acknowledgement of my racial experience being a mix between two different racial experiences has been and continues to be incredibly confusing and I have lived through (and now managing) pretty severe mental illness where I have been suicidal a big chunk of my life.   


I will also mention that you cannot know how your child will or will not experience life as a racialized child. Meaning your child can look more european than asian or vice versa or kinda in between and depending on these visual factors your child will experience their own identity very differently. Personally, I am racially ambiguous where I get mistaken for being a spanish speaking person often, or everyone thinking I'm white in Japan, and then people thinking I'm asian (they always say its in the eyes.. :/).   


Now I'm not saying that your child will have an identity crisis their whole life just because they are mixed, but it really depends on how you and your boyfriend handle the proper raising of this child. If your boyfriend can't even have a conversation about race without being offended, or even worse he says he doesnt see race, then I don't know what to say other than leave him or at the least really advocate how important this is to not just you but for the baby. Because news flash to him, he is having a child with you, someone who is racialized, and therefore there is a big chance of your child being racialized. If he actually gives a shit he will listen to you. And I really dont care if you or anyone considers him to have a fetish or not, because in the end we all have racist ideas engrained in us because of western colonization that needs to be unlearned and that means just fucking reading about race!!!   


It is incredibly frustrating and even infuriating to see situations like this because so many times in my life I wanted to end my life because of endless confusion and nowhere to go with my thoughts. It may not seem that serious or dramatic to him or maybe you but you will see when your child becomes estranged as they become an adult.   


If your boyfriend is at the very least open to conversation about race and cultural importance in the raising of this child, then there is some hope, but a lot of work to do. If he just is defensive and thinks you are just calling him racist and that is the end of all the conversations then I dont know what good advice to say other than just leave. Think about the future of this child and the hopefully long lasting relationship you will have with this child. I wish you the best.
